title: Chapter 2782 - 114: Sishen
content:
Initially, the people of the Barbaric Wilderness might also just think this is a simple famine disaster.

In the history of the Great Wilderness, famines are frequent, and similar accounts are not uncommon.

Most Barbarian Cultivators initially only thought that this famine disaster was the same as before, that some people would starve to death and they would make it through.

Until the famine disaster spread rapidly over a larger area.

The Barbarian Cultivators shrouded by the famine disaster began to experience various anomalies.

Only then did people realize that this might be different...

...

At this moment, in the barren lands of the three thousand Barbaric Wilderness.

A squad of more than six thousand Barbarian Soldiers is advancing like a long dragon.

Mo Hua, being the Shaman who needs to lead the way, is walking at the forefront.

Mo Hua is also closely observing the status of the famine disaster along the way.

After leaving the Wutian Tribe, the scenery along the way is no different than before, still very desolate, but gradually, people can be seen.

These are truly "living" people.

And quite a few are Cultivators from medium-sized tribes.

Seeing this makes Mo Hua slightly relieved.

"Fortunately, there are finally living people..."

Mo Hua begins to send people to approach these surviving tribe Cultivators to understand the situation.

After contacting them, Mo Hua roughly understands why these tribes managed to survive the famine disaster.

Facing disaster, people often have inertia.

They didn't take this famine disaster seriously at first, but as its "strangeness" gradually appeared.

Many tribes realized the problem.

These tribes are generally medium to large tribes, with secluded ancestors, high cultivation Great Chiefs, knowledgeable Chief Elders, and a group of powerful Golden Cores.

The height of their Realm allows them to see the problem better than ordinary Barbarian Cultivators.

Therefore, they also adopted various measures to cope with the famine disaster.

Even going as far as migrating the tribe to avoid disaster.

These measures can't be perfect, and many people died halfway, tribes were scattered, dying from various unknown factors.

Besides predicting the disaster, it's also crucial to see the execution power in response.

If some tribes moved slowly and didn't migrate before the famine disaster spread, the outcome might be bad.

However, with tribal support, there's still a part of the population left alive.

As for ordinary small tribes, those with low Realm can't foresee the arrival of "disaster" and can only rely on fate.

If lucky and just happened to land in the "gap" of the famine, then they can survive.

Like the Wutian Tribe, which managed to do so.

If unlucky and directly swallowed by the famine, then only doomed with the fate of tribal extermination and everyone turned into mummies.

The "famine disaster" is like a "sieve," filtering through the Great Wilderness.

Those who didn't die in the famine were either lucky, or had opportunities, or foresaw the risk.

But surviving is tough.

Mo Hua also tries to unite these surviving Barbarian Cultivators, rallying together to fight against the Heavenly Calamity, in the name of "Shaman" and Dan Zhu.

But most tribes refuse.

Non-my tribe, their hearts are different.

In the Barbaric Wilderness, tribal conflicts are intense and discrepancies are severe, they wouldn't easily trust others.

Especially now with the rampant famine disaster, pledging allegiance to an unfamiliar Mo Hua may result in being treated as "rations."

Mo Hua's "forces under him" are also too strong.

Lie Bone's General in Late Golden Core Stage, plus over ten Golden Core Commanders from the Shugu Tribe.

The Young Master of the Danque Tribe, Dan Zhu, along with Danque Tribe's Barbarian General Chi Feng, and two Golden Core Elders.

Also, the fierce Bone Heavy Armor Soldiers and a six thousand Barbarian Soldiers Alliance.

Such forces in years of famine are almost like a "giant crocodile."

These surviving, scattered tribes, if aligned with Mo Hua's forces, would have no resistance if they were swallowed alive.

If Mo Hua used force, he could forcibly "absorb" these tribes.

But it wouldn't make sense.

With hearts not united, absorption wouldn't work.

Moreover, Mo Hua himself is also in a precarious situation.

If he can maintain his current forces and keep these people alive, it would be a great fortune.

Mo Hua sighed lightly in his heart.

But anyhow, it's good that there are survivors.

With people alive, it proves that the Famine Disaster Formation hasn't completely closed, there are still opportunities in this "Heavenly Calamity"...

"As for Uncle, what exactly does he want to do with this Famine Disaster Formation..."

Mo Hua looks up at the black Death Qi in the sky, with his brows furrowed.

The world is like a chess game, all beings like pieces.

Now the land of the Barbaric Wilderness is the chessboard, countless Barbarian Cultivators are the pieces.

Uncle's pair of dark hands are controlling everything.

And Mo Hua has inadvertently plunged headfirst into Uncle's game...

Mo Hua's heart is heavy, even his Sea of Consciousness feels oppressed.

...

Then Mo Hua continues on his journey, but the pressure in his heart remains firmly pressed against his chest.

The mood of Dan Zhu and others slightly improved.

Along the way, many tribes have some acquaintance with the Danque Tribe, revealing some news about the Danque Tribe.

They learn from these messages that the main body of Danque has temporarily survived. Although the specific situation is unknown, there's no tribal extermination crisis at least.

Dan Zhu and others breathe a sigh of relief, but their desire to return to the tribe grows stronger.

The group continues their journey, for another two days, until they see a stretch of mountains in front.

The famine disaster stands like a miasma before them, enveloping the whole mountain range, blocking the road ahead.

Dan Zhu and others split up to investigate, walking along the mountains to the sides for a long time, but the gas of the famine disaster still stretches endlessly.
